Visualize Link Functions

Source: R/methods.R
plot.link.Rd

autoplot() returns a graph of a link object in two panels, and plot() prints that graph:

  1. the link function \(\eta = g(\theta)\) over its valid domain;

  2. the inverse link function \(\theta = g^{-1}(\eta)\) over a standard range of linear predictors.

Dotted grey lines mark zero on both axes of each panel.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'link'
plot(x, ...)

autoplot.link(object, ...)

Arguments

x, object

An object of class link.

...

Unused; an argument passed here signals an error.

Value

autoplot() returns a patchwork object holding the two ggplot2 panels; plot() prints the same object and returns it invisibly.

Details

The plotting ranges depend on whether the link bounds are finite. A bounded domain is drawn up to a distance of 1e-4 from each finite bound, and an unbounded side extends five units past the other bound (or from \(-5\) to \(5\) when neither bound is finite). The inverse is drawn over the values of \(\eta\) reached in the first panel, restricted to \([-6, 6]\) when the two ranges overlap.

The graph is drawn with ggplot2 and its two panels are joined with patchwork; both packages are suggested, and the methods signal an error that names them when they are not installed. The returned object can be modified like any other, for instance with + patchwork::plot_annotation(title = "my title").

Examples

plot(logit_link())

plot(softplus_link(2))
